name: es32-advanced-blend-and-sample-shading
title: Advanced blend equations and sample shading
summary: All 15 advanced blend equations (MULTIPLY, SCREEN, OVERLAY, DARKEN, LIGHTEN, COLORDODGE, COLORBURN, HARDLIGHT, SOFTLIGHT, DIFFERENCE, EXCLUSION, HSL_HUE, HSL_SATURATION, HSL_COLOR, HSL_LUMINOSITY) blend two overlapping premultiplied discs (alpha 0.45 .. 0.9) over a premultiplied gradient backdrop (alpha 0.45 .. 0.95), separated by glBlendBarrier, each shader declaring layout(blend_support_<equation>) or blend_support_all_equations; every texel is compared with a CPU implementation of ES 3.2 section 15.1.5.3 (Tables 15.3/15.4 and the HSL pseudocode), and the draw-time errors (no or the wrong qualifier, two draw buffers) and the INVALID_ENUM of BlendEquationSeparate are provoked. Sample shading is read back per sample with texelFetch(sampler2DMS): gl_SampleID, gl_NumSamples, gl_SampleMaskIn, gl_SamplePosition against glGetMultisamplefv, the sample qualifier, MinSampleShading 1.0 and 0.5, interpolateAtSample/Offset/Centroid; the picture shows the blend grid over a checkerboard and a ring pattern shaded per pixel and per sample.
spec: ES 3.2 §15.1.5 Blending, §15.1.5.1 Blend Equation (BlendEquation accepts Tables 15.1, 15.3 and 15.4; INVALID_ENUM from BlendEquationSeparate for anything outside Table 15.1; advanced equations computed with at least the smaller of the destination precision and 16-bit float), §15.1.5.3 Advanced Blend Equations (premultiplied inputs, p0/p1/p2, Table 15.3, Table 15.4 and the HSL pseudocode, single color buffer and fragment color zero, INVALID_OPERATION for multiple draw buffers and for a fragment shader without the matching blend_support qualifier while blending is enabled, BlendBarrier and blending passes), §15.1.5.5 Blending State
ES 3.2 §2.3.1 Errors (a command that generates an error is ignored), Appendix A.1 Repeatability and A.3 Invariance Rules (the backdrop is re-drawn to read the destination)

ES 3.2 §13.4 Multisampling (GetMultisamplefv SAMPLE_POSITION in [0, 1], INVALID_VALUE for index >= SAMPLES, inputs qualified sample in are evaluated at the sample location), §13.4.1 Sample Shading (SAMPLE_SHADING, MinSampleShading clamped to [0, 1], at least max(ceil(mss x samples), 1) unique input sets, fraction 1.0 evaluates each sample at its location)

ES 3.2 §14.1 Fragment Shader Variables (centroid/sample interpolation, interpolateAtCentroid/Sample/Offset, MIN/MAX_FRAGMENT_INTERPOLATION_OFFSET and FRAGMENT_INTERPOLATION_OFFSET_BITS), Table 21.41 (MAX_SAMPLES >= 4, interpolation offset limits -0.5 / +0.5 - 1 ULP / 4 bits), Table 21.8 (SAMPLE_SHADING FALSE, MIN_SAMPLE_SHADING_VALUE 0)

ES 3.2 §8.8 Multisample Textures (TexStorage2DMultisample), §9.2.3.1 Multisample Queries (SAMPLES), §11.1.3.3 Multisample Texel Fetches (the sample number of texelFetch is the GetMultisamplefv index), §15.2.1 Selecting Buffers for Writing (DrawBuffers), §16.1.2 ReadPixels

GLSL ES 3.20 §4.4.2 Output Layout Qualifiers (Fragment Outputs: blend_support_* and blend_support_all_equations), §4.3.4 Input Variables (auxiliary qualifiers may differ between stages, the fragment shader's win), §4.5 Interpolation Qualifiers (centroid, sample), §4.7.1 Range and Precision (mediump relative precision 2^-10 for gl_SamplePosition)

GLSL ES 3.20 §7.1.5 Fragment Shader Special Variables (gl_SampleID, gl_SamplePosition, gl_SampleMaskIn, gl_NumSamples; static use of gl_SampleID or gl_SamplePosition makes the shader run per sample), §8.14.2 Interpolation Functions, §8.9.2 Texel Lookup Functions (texelFetch on sampler2DMS), §8.9.1 (textureSize)

api.glBlendEquation: all 15 advanced equations: each grid cell (backdrop, disc A, glBlendBarrier, disc B) equals the CPU model of section 15.1.5.3 in every texel; BLEND_EQUATION_RGB and BLEND_EQUATION_ALPHA both report the equation; with every equation a draw raises INVALID_OPERATION without blend_support or with another equation's qualifier, and none with its own qualifier or blend_support_all_equations; FUNC_ADD control
api.glBlendEquationSeparate: (MULTIPLY, FUNC_ADD) and (FUNC_ADD, HSL_COLOR) raise INVALID_ENUM and leave BLEND_EQUATION_RGB/ALPHA at FUNC_REVERSE_SUBTRACT
api.glBlendBarrier: between the backdrop and disc A and between the overlapping discs A and B: the 174 texels covered by both discs in each cell equal the sequential composition; no error
api.glBlendFunc: (ZERO, ONE_MINUS_SRC_COLOR) is current while the advanced equations blend and has no effect on the compared results (the equations use no factors)
api.glEnable: BLEND (the draw-time errors require it; the control cell with BLEND disabled replaces), SAMPLE_SHADING (per-sample inputs read back), IsEnabled TRUE
api.glDisable: BLEND (an advanced equation with a shader without blend_support draws without error and replaces), SAMPLE_SHADING (IsEnabled FALSE), DITHER
api.glIsEnabled: SAMPLE_SHADING initially FALSE, TRUE after glEnable, FALSE after glDisable
api.glMinSampleShading: 1.0: an ordinary input equals pixel + glGetMultisamplefv position for all 1024 samples; 0.5: at least ceil(0.5 x 4) distinct inputs in every pixel; 0.25 read back, 1.5 and -0.5 clamped to 1.0 and 0.0
api.glGetFloatv: MIN_SAMPLE_SHADING_VALUE (initial 0, 0.25, clamped values), MIN_FRAGMENT_INTERPOLATION_OFFSET <= -0.5, MAX_FRAGMENT_INTERPOLATION_OFFSET >= 0.5 - 2^-bits; the offsets used for interpolateAtOffset reach both limits
api.glGetIntegerv: BLEND_EQUATION_RGB / BLEND_EQUATION_ALPHA for 15 equations and after the rejected BlendEquationSeparate; MAX_SAMPLES >= 4; SAMPLES of the multisample framebuffers (= gl_NumSamples read back); FRAGMENT_INTERPOLATION_OFFSET_BITS >= 4
api.glGetMultisamplefv: SAMPLE_POSITION of every sample in [0, 1] and equal to gl_SamplePosition, to sample-qualified inputs, to interpolateAtSample and to MinSampleShading(1.0) inputs; INVALID_VALUE for index = SAMPLES
api.glGetInternalformativ: TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE / RGBA8 NUM_SAMPLE_COUNTS and SAMPLES choose the sample count (4 where offered); the allocated textures report that count
api.glTexStorage2DMultisample: 16 x 16 and two 32 x 32 RGBA8 textures with fixed sample locations: complete framebuffers, every sample read back with texelFetch
api.glTexStorage2D: RGBA8 targets (grid, two-attachment scratch, sample strip) read back with glReadPixels
api.glFramebufferTexture2D: TEXTURE_2D color attachments 0 and 1, TEXTURE_2D_MULTISAMPLE attachments; completeness checked
api.glDrawBuffers: {COLOR0, COLOR1} and {NONE, COLOR1} make advanced-equation draws fail with INVALID_OPERATION; {COLOR0, NONE} and FUNC_ADD with two buffers draw without error
api.glClearBufferfv: fills color attachment 0 before the rejected draw; the readback shows it unchanged
api.glReadPixels: grid, backdrop, sample strips and the window region of the grid compared with CPU references
api.glDrawArrays: TRIANGLE_STRIP quads and a TRIANGLES triangle for the centroid test; INVALID_OPERATION cases of section 15.1.5.3
api.glUniform2fv: u_corner: the corners of every quad and of the centroid triangle (in pixels), verified through the interpolated positions
api.glUniform1i: u_disc, u_index (interpolateAtSample sample number), sampler units, composite mode
api.glUniform2f: u_offset (interpolateAtOffset), disc centres, cell origins, region rectangles

visual_review.notes: 256x256 captures of radeonsi, llvmpipe and zink viewed (they look identical), plus 800x800, 640x480 and 333x777 on all three. Top 5/8: a 4x4 grid of 64x40 cells separated by dark lines. Each cell has a rainbow backdrop (red to violet from left to right, brighter upwards) that fades into the grey checkerboard towards the right (alpha 0.95 to 0.45), a left disc and an overlapping right disc. The cells differ as expected: MULTIPLY and DARKEN give a dark lens, SCREEN and LIGHTEN brighten, COLORDODGE has a pale glowing lens, COLORBURN a nearly black lens, DIFFERENCE turns the lens magenta-red, the HSL cells keep the backdrop brightness but change hue or saturation, and the control cell (bottom right) shows the raw discs, a violet-blue disc A under a yellow disc B. Bottom 3/8: three ring panels. Left: blocky aliased rings with moire (per-pixel shading). Middle: the same rings with grey-olive in-between texels at the fine outer rings (per-sample shading, averaged). Right: each texel split into 2x2 sample sub-cells, showing the sub-pixel ring structure. At 333x777 and 640x480 everything is stretched to fill the surface, with no gaps and no unexpected black or magenta pixels.
